title: Prove ordinary chat does not invoke tools
goal: Add canonical M8 integration coverage proving ordinary conversational requests that do not express a supported Skill or tool intent do not invoke modules or emit Skill observations.
context: Issue #347 explicitly requires ordinary chat to remain separate from tool execution. Workspace-specific regressions cover many denied and incomplete requests, but a direct positive regression for ordinary non-tool chat should verify the canonical chat Skill and team selection entry points remain inert.
forbidden_changes: Do not change production routing or make ordinary chat execute a Skill.
Do not weaken policy, Agent scope, approval, schema validation, cancellation, workspace restrictions, or verification.
Do not treat a nil return alone as proof that no capability code ran; assert event evidence.
Do not claim physical-device acceptance from CI.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary conversational requests return no matched Skill/team result from the canonical M8 chat entry points.
No moduleInvoked or moduleCompleted event is emitted for those requests.
No observationProduced Skill success/failure event is emitted for those requests.
Existing complete, incomplete, and workspace execution regressions remain unchanged.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: If a test reveals ordinary chat invokes a tool, stop and investigate the routing boundary before changing behavior. If a required CI gate fails, repair only within allowed_paths or revert this logical task; never bypass policy or claim device acceptance.
